## Question 1

a) Come up with an example research question in your field of study that would be "answerable" using moderation in a linear model.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} Briefly describe what the outcome variable is, what the predictor variables are, and (very briefly and non-technically) why we might be scientifically interested in the interaction effect.

b) In your own words, describe what the difference is between a predictor's partial effect in a multiple regression without moderation{{< hp glyph="b" >}} and that same predictor's simple effect in a multiple regression with moderation.


## Question 2

a) Read in the `affairs` dataset and use it to estimate a model that tests whether the relationship between the number of years a participant has been married ($x_1$, `yearsmarried`) and their martial satisfaction ($y$, `satisfaction`) is moderated by their years of education ($x_2$, `education`).

b) Interpret each of the four parameters in terms of whether they are significant and also what the coefficient estimate implies about the relationship between the variables.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} (Note: For interaction effects, correctly stating one of the two equivalent interpretations is enough to earn full credit.)


## Question 3

a) Plot the predictions of this model and describe in your own words what the nature of the interaction is (i.e., how the relationship between `yearsmarried` and `satisfaction` differs based on `education`). (Note that when there are a small number of unique values in a continuous predictor, `predict_response()` will spotlight all of them by default. However, you can optionally tell it to spotlight the mean and one SD above and below it by using `"education[meansd]"` as the second term.)

b) Estimate the slope of `yearsmarried` conditional on education being equal to 12 (high school), 16 (college), and 20 (graduate) years. Which slopes are significant and which aren't?


## Question 4

a) Estimate a model that tests whether the relationship between the number of years a participant has been married ($x_1$, `yearsmarried`) and their martial satisfaction ($y$, `satisfaction`) is moderated by whether they have children ($x_2$, `children`).

b) Interpret each of the four parameters in terms of whether they are significant and also what the coefficient estimate implies about the relationship between the variables.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} *Hint: Although this is not a graded part of the question, it may help you to plot the interaction and/or run contrasts.*


## Question 5

a) Estimate a model that tests whether the difference between participants with and without children ($x_1$, `children`) in martial satisfaction ($y$, `satisfaction`) is moderated by their gender ($x_2$, `gender`).

b) Interpret each of the four parameters in terms of whether they are significant and also what the coefficient estimate implies about the relationship between the variables.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} *Hint: Although this is not a graded part of the question, it may help you to plot the interaction and/or run contrasts.*
